perspective:
**Harold Padilla’s available information:**

- Harold knows he is a project manager whose project progress is suffering. He initially feels frustrated and anxious, believing his team is unmotivated.
- He knows Arthur Begum as a friend and police officer whom he trusts for advice. Harold arranged and attended a coffee-shop meeting with Arthur.
- In that meeting, Harold told Arthur that his team seemed completely unmotivated and that he was at his wit’s end.
- Harold heard Arthur suggest understanding what drives each team member individually, having one-on-one conversations, and making people feel valued and understood personally.
- Harold decided to try Arthur’s advice and felt hopeful and relieved afterward.
- Harold then told his team he wanted one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each of them. He heard Team Member 1 say that could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they were open to it. Harold said he would schedule time with each of them.
- Later, Harold observed that the team still was not responding well to the new strategies. He felt disappointed and worried about the project’s future.
- Harold met Arthur again and told him the suggestions had not worked. He heard Arthur suggest there might be deeper issues, such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold might need to dig deeper.
- Harold decided to hold another round of one-on-one meetings. He told team members he had noticed issues and asked them to share concerns.
- Harold heard Team Member 1 say there was tension between a few team members that was affecting work. He heard Team Member 2 say they felt overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making it hard to stay motivated.
- Harold told them he would look into resolving conflicts, consider redistributing tasks, and that their well-being was important to him.
- Harold then felt optimistic and empowered. He told the team he would implement regular feedback sessions and team-building activities to create a more supportive environment.
- Harold heard Team Member 1 say that sounded great and would help, and Team Member 2 agree that it was good their concerns were being addressed. Harold told them their input and well-being were crucial to the project’s success.

**Not available to Harold:** private thoughts or hidden causes of team members’ behavior beyond what they told him; the exact identities/details of the “tension between a few” unless later revealed; whether Arthur’s suggested possibilities—personal conflicts, lack of trust, external stressors—are actually true; and any narrator-only information or unspoken information about other characters.
